messages.text: 'use proactively' marking found — encourages autonomous delegation

writing.overall_comment: A well-scoped, contract-driven agent definition whose main weakness is redundant restatement of skills and principles that could be trimmed without losing guidance.

dimensions.name: Delegation fit
dimensions.comment: The description names concrete triggers (Fiber APIs, Cobra CLI, GORM, Clean Architecture) so a main agent can route confidently, though it lacks explicit negative triggers like 'not for frontend/infra'.

dimensions.name: Prompt quality
dimensions.comment: Role, tech stack, DO/DON'T constraints, layer ordering, and a concrete output contract (files plus build/test/assumptions report) are all explicit and actionable.

dimensions.name: Boundaries
dimensions.comment: A dedicated Boundaries section states what is out of scope, how to handle schema ambiguity, and precise hand-back conditions including the target agent (system-architect).

dimensions.name: Conciseness
dimensions.comment: The expertise list, Integrated Skills section, and 'When Implementing Features' steps restate the same stack and flow, and three full code examples push the token budget well past what the guidance needs.

suggestions: In the expertise list, Integrated Skills section, and 'When Implementing Features' steps, consolidate the repeated stack and flow descriptions into one shared reference to eliminate redundancy.
In the three full code examples, replace them with a single concise representative example or short snippets to reduce the token budget while preserving the core guidance.
In the Integrated Skills section, merge overlapping skill bullets into the expertise list or a compact table to further shorten the guidance without losing coverage.
